Do you have to register anything?

Do you have to get tags?

Any ridiculous rules in your state?

Here in Colorado you just have to do hunter safety courses and then register for a lottery system that awards tags for specific sexes of specific animals in specific areas (Game management units, or GMUs). There's also over-the-counter tag purchases available after the initial lottery. There's also a little-known roadkill tag where, I guess, if you hit a game animal you can get a tag for it to make harvesting it legal.
What's hunting like where you live?

I hunt in the northeast. There are a lot of annoying laws around here regarding hunting and firearms.

For example, in mass you cannot hunt white tail with a rifle, and if you are bowhunting, you cannot have a sidearm. Also, they don't allow Sunday hunting which is pretty weak.

I also hunt in PA, where semi-automatic rifles are illegal for hunting whitetail.

Tag system for both states is pretty standad, however. Apply and get a tag for a specific sex.

In Illinois you can't hunt whitetail with a rifle either, or carry a sidearm while bow hunting, but then again we don't have bears to worry about and have a lot of flat open land. I've never heard of the Sunday rule before, that reallllly blows. Here in Illinois sometimes public land is closed on certain days, but other than that nothing

I live and hunt in Oklahoma and it's a great state for hunting! I have a lifetime hunting & fishing license so I don't have to get tags. I can't think of any crazy rules here. We have a hunter safety course to pass before getting your license but it was a pretty painless experience from what I remember; I took mine probably 12 years ago.

My parents have 500 acres that my dad keeps up with good food plots to keep the deer bedded on our land and plenty of stands for when season opens. I'd have to say I have it pretty good when it comes to hunting

I will add for the sake of adding.

I hunt Arizona and Utah once in a great while as well as some of the tribal lands in AZ.

In AZ we have units and the same goes for tribal lands. Arizona has lottery draw where every year you put in and don't get drawn you gain 1 point. These points help you next year and the year after. Once you get drawn your points are cleared and begin again.

On tribal lands the drawing can be far more difficult to obtain but when you are drawn you better make the most of it. If you are putting in as a non-tribal hunt applicant the prices can run into the thousands of dollars.

The hunting is great but you can not be lazy and expect to fill your tag. A lot of hiking, spot and stalk as well as huge swings in weather makes it fun and challenging. I hunt rifle, archery and shot gun for birds. The only restrictions we have is minimum poundage on the bow and a minimum caliber on the rifles. Firearms are also restricted to no for than 5 rounds in a magazine or 3 rounds in your shotgun.
